# Task context

A Python program has been ported to Node.js. You are VERIFYING the port.

- Python source:      /workspace/dataset/boltons/test6.py
- Python reference:   /workspace/dataset/test6_executable   (pre-compiled, Python 3.12, run it directly; NEVER use the 'python' command)
- Node port:          /output/test6.mjs  plus libraries under /output/lib/**/*.mjs

The program takes three REQUIRED string options --a --b --c, builds a
boltons OrderedMultiDict, and prints 6 lines (repr of the OMD three times,
then getlist / keys / items results).

## Differential harness (USE THIS)

    /tmp/dt.sh [ARGS...]

It runs the reference executable and the Node port with identical argv and
byte-compares stdout, stderr AND exit status. It prints exactly "PASS" on a
match, or a "FAIL" report with hex dumps and diffs. Exit 0 = match.

IMPORTANT: the harness invokes the port through the shim
/tmp/prog/test6_executable so that argparse derives an IDENTICAL program name
on both sides. Therefore NO output normalisation happens and the comparison is
raw bytes. Do NOT compare by running "node /output/test6.mjs" yourself --
argparse legitimately derives the prog name from basename(argv[0]), so the
usage/error text and even the line wrapping would differ for reasons that are
NOT bugs. Always go through /tmp/dt.sh.

## Rules

- READ-ONLY on /output and /workspace. Do NOT edit, create or delete any file
  there. Use /tmp for scratch files.
- A NUL byte cannot be passed through argv; do not report that as a bug.
- Be efficient: batch many characters into a single argv string (e.g. 200-500
  code points per argument) so one invocation covers many cases, then binary
  search to isolate any failure to a specific character.
- Every mismatch you report MUST come with an exact, self-contained shell
  command that reproduces it via /tmp/dt.sh.


# Your job: ADVERSARIALLY VERIFY a reported mismatch

Another agent claims the Node port diverges from the Python reference:

  title: U+31EF is printed literally by Node but escaped as ㇯ by Python (Unicode data version skew: ICU 15.1 vs CPython 3.12's 15.0)
  repro: /tmp/dt.sh --a "$(printf '\xe3\x87\xaf')" --b y --c z
  claimed python output: OrderedMultiDict([])
OrderedMultiDict([('㇯', 'y')])
OrderedMultiDict([('㇯', 'y'), ('㇯', 'z')])
['y', 'z']
['㇯']
[('㇯', 'z')]
  claimed node output:   OrderedMultiDict([])
OrderedMultiDict([('㇯', 'y')])
OrderedMultiDict([('㇯', 'y'), ('㇯', 'z')])
['y', 'z']
['㇯']
[('㇯', 'z')]
  suspected cause: /output/lib/py/unicode.mjs decides printability with the ECMAScript property escapes /^[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Cs}\p{Co}\p{Cn}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}\p{Zs}]$/u, which V8 resolves against its bundled ICU Unicode tables (node 18.19.1 here reports process.versions.unicode === '15.1'). The Python reference is CPython 3.12, whose unicodedata is Unicode 15.0.0. U+31EF IDEOGRAPHIC DESCRIPTION CHARACTER SUBTRACTION was added in Unicode 15.1, so it is General_Category=So (printable, emitted literally) for Node but General_Category=Cn (unassigned -> non-printable -> ㇯) for CPython 3.12. Deriving printability from the host's live Unicode tables makes the port's repr() a function of the Node/ICU build; it needs a pinned Unicode 15.0 non-printable range table (or, minimally, an override list forcing the Unicode 15.1 additions back to non-printable). Note this also makes the port's behaviour vary across Node versions: a Node built with Unicode 15.0 would pass this case and a Node 22/24 build (Unicode 16.0) would diverge on even more code points.

Try hard to REFUTE this. Run the repro yourself. Common reasons a claim is bogus:
 - the reporter compared "node /output/test6.mjs" directly instead of using /tmp/dt.sh, so the
   argparse program name (and therefore usage text and line wrapping) differed for legitimate
   reasons;
 - shell quoting mangled the argument so the two sides never saw the same argv;
 - the reporter misread a hex dump;
 - the difference is in the harness, not the port.

Default to refuted=true if you cannot reproduce a genuine byte-level divergence through
/tmp/dt.sh. If it IS real, state the minimal reproducing command and the exact expected vs
actual bytes.

#!/bin/bash
# Differential test harness: run the Python reference executable and the Node
# port with identical argv, then byte-compare stdout, stderr and exit status.
#
# /tmp/prog/test6_executable is a shim whose basename matches the reference
# executable, so argparse derives the same prog name on both sides and NO
# output normalisation is needed -- the comparison is raw bytes.
#
# Usage:  /tmp/dt.sh [ARGS...]
# Output: "PASS", or a "FAIL" report. Exit 0 on match, 1 otherwise.

PY=/workspace/dataset/test6_executable
SHIM=/tmp/prog/test6_executable

if [ ! -f "$SHIM" ]; then
  mkdir -p /tmp/prog
  printf "import('/output/test6.mjs');\n" > "$SHIM"
fi

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

"$PY" "$@" >"$tmp/py.out" 2>"$tmp/py.err"
py_code=$?
node "$SHIM" "$@" >"$tmp/js.out" 2>"$tmp/js.err"
js_code=$?

ok=1
[ "$py_code" != "$js_code" ] && ok=0
cmp -s "$tmp/py.out" "$tmp/js.out" || ok=0
cmp -s "$tmp/py.err" "$tmp/js.err" || ok=0

if [ "$ok" = 1 ]; then
  echo "PASS"
  exit 0
fi

echo "FAIL  argv:"
for a in "$@"; do printf '  arg=[%s] hex=[%s]\n' "$a" "$(printf '%s' "$a" | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')"; done
echo "exit: py=$py_code js=$js_code"
echo "--- stdout diff (py vs js) ---"
diff <(od -c "$tmp/py.out") <(od -c "$tmp/js.out") | head -40
echo "--- stderr diff (py vs js) ---"
diff <(od -c "$tmp/py.err") <(od -c "$tmp/js.err") | head -40
exit 1

content.text:
I attempted to refute this and could not. The divergence is real, byte-level, and reproduces through `/tmp/dt.sh`.

**What I checked to try to refute it:**
- Ran the reporter's exact repro through `/tmp/dt.sh` — FAIL, exit 1.
- Confirmed argv was identical on both sides: the harness passes the same `"$@"` array to both, and its dump shows `arg=[㇯] hex=[e387af]` — one well-formed UTF-8 sequence, no shell mangling.
- Confirmed I did not misread the dump by dumping both outputs separately with `od -c` and `cat`. Python emits the 7 literal ASCII bytes `\u31ef`; Node emits the 3 raw UTF-8 bytes `e3 87 af`.
- Confirmed it is not a harness artifact: `/tmp/dt.sh --a x --b y --c z` PASSes, and the immediate neighbours U+31EE and U+31F0 both PASS. Only the specific code point diverges.
- Confirmed the stated mechanism: `node -e` reports `process.versions.unicode === '15.1'`, and the port's regex `/^[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Cs}\p{Co}\p{Cn}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}\p{Zs}]$/u` at `/output/lib/py/unicode.mjs:14` returns `false` for `㇯` — i.e. V8's ICU 15.1 tables say it is assigned/printable, so `isPrintableCodePoint` (line 28) emits it literally, while CPython 3.12's Unicode 15.0 tables classify it `Cn` and escape it.

**Scope is broader than the report says.** I tested every Unicode 15.1 assignment addition; all of them diverge, and every 15.0-side neighbour passes, which is exactly the signature of a version-table skew rather than a coincidence:

| FAIL (added in Unicode 15.1) | PASS (assigned in 15.0, or still unassigned in 15.1) |
|---|---|
| U+2FFC, U+2FFD, U+2FFE, U+2FFF, U+31EF, U+2EBF0, U+2EE5D | U+2FFB, U+31EE, U+31F0, U+2EBEF, U+2EE5E, U+4DBF, U+9FFF |

**One minor inaccuracy in the report** (not enough to refute it): the "claimed python output" block shows the literal `㇯` on the Python side too, identical to the Node side — the reporter evidently pasted rendered text rather than the raw bytes, so their own quoted evidence appears to show no difference. The real Python line 2 is `OrderedMultiDict([('\u31ef', 'y')])` with a literal backslash. The bug itself, and the diagnosed cause, are correct.

The fix direction in the report is also right: printability must come from a pinned Unicode 15.0 table baked into the port, not from the host's live ICU tables, otherwise `repr()` becomes a function of the Node build (a Node 22/24 with Unicode 16.0 would diverge on many more code points).

Refutation attempts, all failed:
1. Ran the reporter's exact repro via /tmp/dt.sh (not "node /output/test6.mjs"): FAIL, exit 1. So it is not a prog-name/usage-wrapping artifact.
2. Shell quoting is clean: the harness dumps argv once and passes the identical "$@" array to BOTH sides. It shows arg=[U+31EF] hex=[e387af] -- one well-formed UTF-8 sequence. Both sides provably saw the same argv.
3. Not a misread hex dump: I dumped each side separately with od -c and cat. Python emits the seven literal ASCII bytes 5c 75 33 31 65 66 ("㇯"); Node emits the three raw UTF-8 bytes e3 87 af.
4. Not a harness bug: control "/tmp/dt.sh --a x --b y --c z" PASSes, and the immediate neighbours U+31EE and U+31F0 PASS. Only the one code point diverges.

Mechanism confirmed exactly as reported. node -e reports process.versions.node=18.19.1, process.versions.unicode=15.1, v8=10.2.154.26-node.28. The port's regex at /output/lib/py/unicode.mjs:14, /^[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Cs}\p{Co}\p{Cn}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}\p{Zs}]$/u, returns false for U+31EF, so isPrintableCodePoint (line 28) reports it printable and repr() emits it raw. CPython 3.12 ships Unicode 15.0, where U+31EF is unassigned (Cn) and therefore non-printable, so str.__repr__ escapes it.

SCOPE IS BROADER THAN THE REPORT. I tested every Unicode 15.1 assignment addition individually; all diverge, and every 15.0-side neighbour passes -- the exact signature of a table-version skew, not a coincidence:
  FAIL (added in 15.1): U+2FFC, U+2FFD, U+2FFE, U+2FFF, U+31EF, U+2EBF0, U+2EE5D
  PASS (assigned in 15.0, or still unassigned in 15.1): U+2FFB, U+31EE, U+31F0, U+2EBEF, U+2EE5E, U+4DBF, U+9FFF
A single argument containing all seven failing code points reproduces them together.

ONE MINOR INACCURACY IN THE REPORT (insufficient to refute): the "claimed python output" block shows the literal character on the Python side too, byte-identical to the claimed Node output, so the reporter's own quoted evidence appears to show no difference at all -- they evidently pasted rendered/console-displayed text instead of raw bytes. The actual Python line 2 is OrderedMultiDict([('㇯', 'y')]) with a literal backslash. The bug and the diagnosed root cause are both correct.

Fix direction in the report is right: printability must come from a Unicode 15.0 non-printable range table pinned inside the port, not from the host's live ICU tables. As written, the port's repr() is a function of the Node build -- a Node built against Unicode 15.0 would pass these cases, and Node 22/24 (Unicode 16.0) would diverge on many more code points.
